title: 亚马逊如何说明返办公室安排和组织比例目标（2024）
topic: 准确转述一封旧员工信中的到岗日期、例外和组织比例目标

source.title: Update from Amazon CEO Andy Jassy on return-to-office plans and manager team ratio
source.license: 原文按项目方确认的授权收录
source.context: 基于 Amazon CEO 2024 年员工邮件；返办公室安排和组织比例目标均有明确生效时间，属于历史政策信息。
paragraphs: So, we’re asking each s-team organization to increase the ratio of individual contributors to managers by at least 15% by the end of Q1 2025.

But, before the pandemic, it was not a given that folks could work remotely two days a week, and that will also be true moving forward—our expectation is that people will be in the office outside of extenuating circumstances (like the ones mentioned above) or if you already have a Remote Work Exception approved through your s-team leader.
To help ensure a smooth transition, we’re going to make this new expectation active on January 2, 2025.
translations: 因此，我们要求各 S-team 组织在 2025 年第一季度末前，将个人贡献者与经理的比例至少提高 15%。
不过，疫情前并没有“每周可以远程办公两天”的默认安排，今后也一样——除上述特殊情况外，员工应到办公室工作；如果已经通过所属 S-team 负责人获批远程工作例外，也可以远程办公。
为确保平稳过渡，我们会在 2025 年 1 月 2 日让这项新要求正式生效。
fullTextParagraphs: The message below was shared with Amazon employees today.
Hey team. I wanted to send a note on a couple changes we’re making to further strengthen our culture and teams.

First, for perspective, I feel good about the progress we’re making together. Stores, AWS, and Advertising continue to grow on very large bases, Prime Video continues to expand, and new investment areas like GenAI, Kuiper, Healthcare, and several others are evolving nicely. And at the same time we’re growing and inventing, we’re also continuing to make progress on our cost structure and operating margins, which isn’t easy to do. Overall, I like the direction in which we’re heading and appreciate the hard work and ingenuity of our teams globally.

When I think about my time at Amazon, I never imagined I’d be at the company for 27 years. My plan (which my wife and I agreed to on a bar napkin in 1997) was to be here a few years and move back to NYC. Part of why I’ve stayed has been the unprecedented growth (we had $15M of annual revenue the year before I joined—this year should be well north of $600B), the perpetual hunger to invent, the obsession with making customers’ lives easier and better every day, and the associated opportunities these priorities present. But, the biggest reason I’m still here is our culture. Being so customer focused is an inspiring part of it, but it’s also the people we work with, the way we collaborate and invent when we’re at our best, our long-term perspective, the ownership I’ve always felt at every level I’ve worked (I started as a Level 5), the speed with which we make decisions and move, and the lack of bureaucracy and politics.

Our culture is unique, and has been one of the most critical parts of our success in our first 29 years. But, keeping your culture strong is not a birthright. You have to work at it all the time. When you consider the breadth of our businesses, their associated growth rates, the innovation required across each of them, and the number of people we’ve hired the last 6-8 years to pursue these endeavors, it’s pretty unusual—and will stretch even the strongest of cultures. Strengthening our culture remains a top priority for the s-team and me. And, I think about it all the time.

We want to operate like the world’s largest startup. That means having a passion for constantly inventing for customers, strong urgency (for most big opportunities, it’s a race!), high ownership, fast decision-making, scrappiness and frugality, deeply-connected collaboration (you need to be joined at the hip with your teammates when inventing and solving hard problems), and a shared commitment to each other.

Two areas that the s-team and I have been thinking about the last several months are: 1/ do we have the right org structure to drive the level of ownership and speed we desire? 2/ are we set up to invent, collaborate, and be connected enough to each other (and our culture) to deliver the absolute best for customers and the business that we can? We think we can be better on both.

On the first topic, we’ve always sought to hire very smart, high judgment, inventive, delivery-focused, and missionary teammates. And, we have always wanted the people doing the actual detailed work to have high ownership. As we have grown our teams as quickly and substantially as we have the last many years, we have understandably added a lot of managers. In that process, we have also added more layers than we had before. It’s created artifacts that we’d like to change (e.g., pre-meetings for the pre-meetings for the decision meetings, a longer line of managers feeling like they need to review a topic before it moves forward, owners of initiatives feeling less like they should make recommendations because the decision will be made elsewhere, etc.). Most decisions we make are two-way doors, and as such, we want more of our teammates feeling like they can move fast without unnecessary processes, meetings, mechanisms, and layers that create overhead and waste valuable time.

So, we’re asking each s-team organization to increase the ratio of individual contributors to managers by at least 15% by the end of Q1 2025. Having fewer managers will remove layers and flatten organizations more than they are today. If we do this work well, it will increase our teammates’ ability to move fast, clarify and invigorate their sense of ownership, drive decision-making closer to the front lines where it most impacts customers (and the business), decrease bureaucracy, and strengthen our organizations’ ability to make customers’ lives better and easier every day. We will do this thoughtfully, and our PxT team will work closely with our leaders to evolve our organizations to accomplish these goals over the next few months.

[By the way, I’ve created a “Bureaucracy Mailbox” for any examples any of you see where we might have bureaucracy or unnecessary process that’s crept in and we can root out…to be clear, companies need process to run effectively, and process does not equal bureaucracy, but unnecessary and excessive process or rules should be called out and extinguished. I will read these emails and action them accordingly.]

To address the second issue of being better set up to invent, collaborate, and be connected enough to each other and our culture to deliver the absolute best for customers and the business, we’ve decided that we’re going to return to being in the office the way we were before the onset of COVID. When we look back over the last five years, we continue to believe that the advantages of being together in the office are significant. I’ve previously explained these benefits (February 2023 post), but in summary, we’ve observed that it’s easier for our teammates to learn, model, practice, and strengthen our culture; collaborating, brainstorming, and inventing are simpler and more effective; teaching and learning from one another are more seamless; and, teams tend to be better connected to one another. If anything, the last 15 months we’ve been back in the office at least three days a week has strengthened our conviction about the benefits.

Before the pandemic, not everybody was in the office five days a week, every week. If you or your child were sick, if you had some sort of house emergency, if you were on the road seeing customers or partners, if you needed a day or two to finish coding in a more isolated environment, people worked remotely. This was understood, and will be moving forward as well. But, before the pandemic, it was not a given that folks could work remotely two days a week, and that will also be true moving forward—our expectation is that people will be in the office outside of extenuating circumstances (like the ones mentioned above) or if you already have a Remote Work Exception approved through your s-team leader.

We are also going to bring back assigned desk arrangements in locations that were previously organized that way, including the U.S. headquarters locations (Puget Sound and Arlington). For locations that had agile desk arrangements before the pandemic, including much of Europe, we will continue to operate that way.

We understand that some of our teammates may have set up their personal lives in such a way that returning to the office consistently five days per week will require some adjustments. To help ensure a smooth transition, we’re going to make this new expectation active on January 2, 2025. Global Real Estate and Facilities (GREF) is working on a plan to accommodate desk arrangements mentioned above and will communicate the details as they are finalized.

I want to thank our leaders and support teams in advance for the work they will do to improve their org structures over the coming months. With a company of our size and complexity, the work won’t be trivial and it will test our collective ability to invent and simplify when it comes to how we organize and go after the meaningful opportunities we have across all of our businesses.

Having the right culture at Amazon is something I don’t take for granted. I continue to believe that we are all here because we want to make a difference in customers’ lives, invent on their behalf, and move quickly to solve their problems. I’m optimistic that these changes will better help us accomplish these goals while strengthening our culture and the effectiveness of our teams.

notes.phrase: increase the ratio of individual contributors to managers by at least 15%
notes.meaning: 将个人贡献者与经理的比例至少提高 15%
notes.explain: 这是比例目标，不等于裁掉 15% 的经理，也没有规定从三层减到两层。邮件把截止时间另列为 2025 年第一季度末。
notes.example: The plan aims to increase the ratio of individual contributors to managers by 10% next year.

notes.explain: extenuating circumstances 指会影响正常安排的特殊情况。这里还保留已获批的远程工作例外，不能简化成“任何人都必须每天到办公室”。
notes.example: The team will meet in person outside of extenuating circumstances.

notes.phrase: make this new expectation active on January 2, 2025
notes.meaning: 让这项新要求于 2025 年 1 月 2 日生效
notes.explain: make + 事物 + active 表示让某项安排开始生效；这是 2024 年邮件里的历史日期，转述时要核实当前政策。
notes.example: We will make the updated process active on June 1.

scenario.title: 准确复述旧邮件中的日期与组织目标
english: A teammate asks what Andy Jassy’s 2024 message said about office attendance and the manager-to-individual-contributor ratio.

The five-day office expectation was scheduled to become active on January 2, 2025, with exceptions for extenuating circumstances or an approved Remote Work Exception. Separately, each S-team organization was asked to increase its individual-contributor-to-manager ratio by at least 15% by the end of Q1 2025.
Summarize both dated targets without presenting them as current policy or changing the ratio goal into a fixed number of manager cuts.
chinese: 一位同事问，Andy Jassy 2024 年的邮件如何说明到办公室工作以及经理与个人贡献者的比例。
每周五天到办公室的要求原定于 2025 年 1 月 2 日生效，特殊情况或已获批的远程工作例外除外。另一个目标是，各 S-team 组织在 2025 年第一季度末前将个人贡献者与经理的比例至少提高 15%。
概括这两个带日期的目标，不把它们说成当前政策，也不要把比例目标改说成必须裁掉固定数量的经理。

firstAttempt.prompt: 同事找到 Amazon 2024 年的员工信，想据此安排今年的到岗时间。请用英文说明邮件写的生效日期和例外，并提醒先核实当前政策。
firstAttempt.sample: The 2024 email set the five-day office expectation to start on January 2, 2025, with exceptions for extenuating circumstances or approved remote-work exceptions. Since that date has passed, could we confirm the current policy with HR before making plans?
firstAttempt.rationale: 先准确转述原邮件中的日期和例外，再提醒同事核实现在仍适用的安排。

words.example: The message set a new expectation for office attendance.
words.translation: 这封邮件对到办公室工作提出了新要求。
words.note: 这里指组织希望员工遵循的安排，不表示无例外的命令。

words.example: A family emergency may be an extenuating circumstance.
words.translation: 家庭突发情况可能构成特殊情况。
words.note: 常与 circumstances 连用，说明某种情况需要被纳入考虑。

words.collocation: an approved exception / make an exception
words.example: She has an approved remote-work exception.
words.translation: 她获批了远程工作例外。
words.note: approved 表示已经获批，不能自行推断任何人都符合例外条件。

words.collocation: the ratio of A to B
words.example: The ratio of individual contributors to managers increased.
words.translation: 个人贡献者与经理的比例提高了。
words.note: 邮件写的是两类员工之间的比例，不是直接减少固定数量的经理。

words.meaning: 个人贡献者；非管理岗位员工
words.example: The organization compared individual contributors with managers.
words.translation: 该组织比较了个人贡献者与经理的人数比例。
words.note: 在这里指不担任管理职务、直接承担专业工作的员工。

words.example: The new schedule became active on January 2.
words.translation: 新安排于 1 月 2 日生效。
words.note: 结合日期使用时可说明规则或安排何时开始适用。

structure.original: To help ensure a smooth transition, we’re going to make this new expectation active on January 2, 2025.
analysis: To help ensure a smooth transition 是目的状语，说明采取安排的目的。
we’re going to make... 是将来计划；make + 宾语 + active 表示让某项安排生效。
on January 2, 2025 给出具体生效日期；这是原邮件的历史信息。
structure.transfer: To give the team time to prepare, we’re going to make the updated expense process active on June 1.

rewrite.bad: Amazon cut one manager for every three employees, and everyone had to work in the office starting immediately.
rewrite.good: The 2024 email set the five-day office expectation to start on January 2, 2025, with specified exceptions. It also asked each S-team organization to raise its individual-contributor-to-manager ratio by at least 15% by the end of Q1 2025. We should confirm what applies now.
rewrite.translation: 2024 年邮件把每周五天到办公室的要求定为 2025 年 1 月 2 日开始，并保留特定例外。邮件还要求各 S-team 组织在 2025 年第一季度末前，将个人贡献者与经理的比例至少提高 15%。我们应确认现在适用的安排。
rewrite.pattern: The message set [expectation] to become active on [date], with [exception]. It also asked [group] to change [ratio] by [deadline]. Let’s confirm what applies now.

cloze.prompt: Amazon said the five-day office expectation would become active on ___.
cloze.why: 邮件明确写的是 2025 年 1 月 2 日，不是“立即生效”。

cloze.prompt: People were expected to be in the office outside of extenuating ___.
cloze.why: extenuating circumstances 指特殊情况；邮件还提到了已获批的远程工作例外。

cloze.prompt: Each S-team organization was asked to increase the ratio by at least ___%.
cloze.why: 原文写的是比例至少提高 15%，不是裁减 15% 的经理。

dictation.text: To help ensure a smooth transition, we’re going to make this new expectation active on January 2, 2025.
dictation.label: 听写 1 · 到岗要求的生效日期
dictation.why: 逐字核对邮件给出的生效日期，不把历史安排说成现行政策。

dictation.text: So, we’re asking each s-team organization to increase the ratio of individual contributors to managers by at least 15% by the end of Q1 2025.
dictation.label: 听写 2 · 组织比例目标与期限
dictation.why: 保留提高的对象、幅度和截止时间；邮件没有规定固定裁掉多少名经理。

apply.prompt: 用英文概括邮件中的组织比例目标和期限。
apply.sample: The email asked each S-team organization to increase its individual-contributor-to-manager ratio by at least 15% by the end of Q1 2025.

translationPractice.prompt: 这封 2024 年的邮件把每周五天到办公室的要求定为 2025 年 1 月 2 日生效。
translationPractice.answer: The 2024 email set the five-day office expectation to become active on January 2, 2025.
translationPractice.why: set...to become active on... 表达邮件中安排的生效日期。

translationPractice.prompt: 除特殊情况或已获批的远程工作例外外，员工应到办公室工作。
translationPractice.answer: People were expected to be in the office outside of extenuating circumstances or an approved Remote Work Exception.
translationPractice.why: outside of...说明一般规则的适用范围，同时保留邮件列出的例外。

translationPractice.prompt: 各 S-team 组织需在 2025 年第一季度末前，将个人贡献者与经理的比例至少提高 15%。
translationPractice.answer: Each S-team organization was asked to increase the ratio of individual contributors to managers by at least 15% by the end of Q1 2025.
translationPractice.why: 准确保留比例变化、目标组织和截止时间，不把它改成固定裁员人数。

choice.prompt: 同事把邮件中的组织目标概括成“每个团队必须裁掉 15% 的经理”。哪句最准确地纠正了他？
options: Each S-team organization was asked to increase its individual-contributor-to-manager ratio by at least 15% by the end of Q1 2025; the message did not specify a fixed number of managers to cut.
Every Amazon team had to remove exactly 15 managers by January 2, 2025.
Amazon asked each team to reduce the number of individual contributors by 15% before the return-to-office date.
choice.why: 邮件规定提高个人贡献者与经理的比例至少 15%，并给出第一季度末的期限；没有规定每队裁掉固定人数。

output.prompt: 一位同事找到一份 2024 年的供应商安全流程，准备按它安排今天的供应商上线。请用英文提醒他核实流程是否仍有效，并建议先向 InfoSec 确认当前要求。
output.sample: That document describes the process at the time. Since it is from 2024, could we confirm the current vendor security requirements with InfoSec before scheduling the launch?
check: 是否说明旧文件描述的是当时的流程？
是否提出先确认目前是否仍适用？
是否明确向 InfoSec 核实现行要求？

credits.audio: 美式英语合成朗读，非公司员工原声。

taskPhrases.word: set an expectation to become active on [date]
taskPhrases.meaning: 说明安排从哪一天起生效
taskPhrases.collocation: set + expectation / process + to become active on + date
taskPhrases.example: The 2024 email set the five-day office expectation to become active on January 2, 2025.
taskPhrases.translation: 这封 2024 年的邮件把每周五天到办公室的要求定为 2025 年 1 月 2 日生效。

taskPhrases.meaning: 说明一般规则适用，但特殊情况除外
taskPhrases.example: People were expected to be in the office outside of extenuating circumstances or an approved Remote Work Exception.
taskPhrases.translation: 除特殊情况或已获批的远程工作例外外，员工应到办公室工作。

taskPhrases.word: increase the ratio of A to B by at least X%
taskPhrases.meaning: 说明两个群体之间的比例至少提高多少
taskPhrases.collocation: increase the ratio of + group A + to + group B + by + percentage
taskPhrases.example: Each S-team organization was asked to increase the ratio of individual contributors to managers by at least 15% by the end of Q1 2025.
taskPhrases.translation: 各 S-team 组织需在 2025 年第一季度末前，将个人贡献者与经理的比例至少提高 15%。
